name: Eberstein Castle
architectural_style: Medieval fortress founded 1272; hotel occupies an adjacent 17th–19th-century manor building rather than the castle itself; privately restored since 2000

accessibility: A hillside estate with the hotel in a manor building adjacent to the medieval castle; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: 700 years above the Murg valley — but the hotel occupies an adjacent manor building, not the medieval castle, which now anchors a Michelin-starred restaurant and tavern instead

Hotel rooms are in an adjacent manor building rather than the medieval castle itself — some rooms look directly into the historic castle courtyard rather than being part of it

description:
Eberstein Castle has stood above the Murg valley in Baden-Württemberg for more than 700 years, founded in 1272 by Otto I of Eberstein on a rocky outcrop roughly 130 metres above the valley floor, at the point where the deeply cut middle Murgtal opens into the broader valley around Gernsbach. From the 17th century the castle belonged to the Margraves of Baden, a period of aristocratic ownership that lasted until the year 2000, when the estate passed into private hands and underwent careful restoration.

Today's hotel occupies an adjacent manor building rather than the medieval castle structure itself — guests in the Komfort category rooms look directly into the historic castle courtyard rather than sleeping within its walls. This is a meaningful distinction for anyone booking specifically for a "sleep inside the castle" experience: the historic Eberstein fortress itself functions today primarily as a dramatic backdrop and dining setting, anchored by a Michelin-starred restaurant and a more casual castle tavern, both open to the public and drawing diners independent of the hotel trade.

Otto I of Eberstein's original 13th-century fortification reflects the broader pattern of Staufer-era castle building across the Black Forest's eastern foothills, where numerous small noble lines established fortified positions overlooking the region's river valleys to control trade routes and assert territorial authority. The Ebersteins themselves gave their name to the surrounding area and remained a locally significant noble family for generations before the property passed to the more powerful Margraves of Baden.

The nearly 400 years of Baden margravial ownership, from the 17th century until 2000, gave Eberstein a long institutional continuity under a single ruling house, a pattern shared with several of Baden-Württemberg's other historic castles and residences that remained tied to the Baden dynasty well into the modern era before eventual sale or transfer to private or public hands.

The distinction between the historic castle building and the adjacent hotel manor is worth understanding clearly before booking: while some castle-hotels in this collection house at least some guests within a genuinely medieval structure, Eberstein represents a case where the medieval fortress itself has been preserved specifically as a dining and scenic centerpiece rather than converted into guest accommodation, with the manor building handling the hospitality function instead.

The Michelin-starred restaurant's Baden-French cuisine reflects the wider culinary reputation of the Baden region, historically influenced by its proximity to Alsace and the French border, giving Eberstein's dining offering a genuinely different character from the more traditionally German menus found at some other castle-hotels in this collection.

The northern Black Forest surrounding Eberstein offers extensive hiking terrain directly accessible from the estate, and nearby Baden-Baden's spa town — one of Europe's most historic thermal-bathing destinations — gives guests staying at Eberstein an easy pairing of forest scenery, castle architecture and spa-town culture within a compact area of Baden-Württemberg.

The estate's own vineyards, planted with Riesling and Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir) varietals typical of Baden's warmer, more southerly wine-growing conditions compared to the Rhine and Moselle valleys further north, give Eberstein's terrace and dining rooms a direct visual connection to the wine that frequently accompanies the restaurant's Baden-French menu.
history: Eberstein Castle was founded in 1272 by Otto I of Eberstein above the Murg valley in Baden-Württemberg. From the 17th century it belonged to the Margraves of Baden until the estate passed into private hands in 2000 and underwent careful restoration. Today's hotel occupies an adjacent manor building rather than the medieval castle itself, which now houses a Michelin-starred restaurant and a more casual castle tavern, both open to the public.

faqs.question: Do hotel guests at Eberstein Castle sleep inside the medieval fortress?
faqs.answer: No — the hotel occupies an adjacent manor building rather than the medieval castle structure. Some rooms look directly into the historic castle courtyard, but the fortress itself functions as the estate's restaurant and dining setting rather than guest accommodation.

faqs.question: Can I dine at Eberstein Castle without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — both the Michelin-starred restaurant and the more casual castle tavern (Schlossschänke) are open to non-resident diners by reservation.

faqs.question: How long did the Margraves of Baden own Eberstein Castle?
faqs.answer: From the 17th century until the year 2000, when the estate passed into private hands and underwent restoration — nearly 400 years of ownership by the Baden ruling house.

meta_description: Stay at Eberstein Castle near Baden-Baden — 700 years above the Murg valley, with a Michelin-starred restaurant anchoring the historic fortress itself.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The castle tavern (Schlossschänke) and the Michelin-starred restaurant are open to non-resident diners by reservation. No standing ticketed museum/tour product was found — access beyond dining is for hotel guests.
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Obertsrot, part of Gernsbach, in the Murg valley (Murgtal), Baden-Württemberg; about 20 minutes from Baden-Baden and 30 minutes from Karlsruhe by car.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €189/night, rising to roughly €250+ for larger rooms and suites (verify against live rate). Rooms are in the adjacent manor building, not the medieval castle itself — some overlook the historic castle courtyard.

**On-site:** Michelin-starred restaurant, castle tavern (Schlossschänke), vineyard-view terrace.

**Good to know:** This is a case where the hotel rooms are not within the historic castle structure — the medieval Eberstein fortress itself is the dining and scenic centerpiece of the estate rather than the guest accommodation.

**Combine with:** Baden-Baden's spa town centre and the northern Black Forest (Schwarzwald) hiking trails, both a short drive away.
